learning_objective: 🎯 Learn about the invisible biological systems—nutrition, respiration, transportation, and excretion—that work 24/7 to keep organisms alive!

main_concepts.simple_explanation: Autotrophs (plants) make their own food using sunlight, CO₂, and water via Photosynthesis. Heterotrophs (animals) depend on others for food. Human digestion involves breaking down complex food into simple glucose, amino acids, and fatty acids using enzymes.

Respiration releases energy (ATP) from food. Aerobic respiration requires Oxygen (happens in mitochondria). Anaerobic respiration happens without oxygen (causes lactic acid buildup in muscles during heavy exercise).
The human heart is a 4-chambered pump. It pumps deoxygenated blood to the lungs, and oxygenated blood to the rest of the body. This is called 'Double Circulation'.
Plants use 'Xylem' tissue to transport water and minerals from roots to leaves (driven by transpiration pull). They use 'Phloem' tissue to transport food (sugar) from leaves to the rest of the plant.
The removal of toxic metabolic waste from the body. In humans, the kidneys filter the blood using tiny units called 'Nephrons' to produce urine.

fun_activity.title: 🌿 The Leaf Sweat Test
fun_activity.instructions: Tie a clear plastic bag around a leafy branch of a plant in the sun. Check back in a few hours. You will see water droplets inside the bag. This is 'Transpiration'—plants sweating out excess water!

exam_tips: 📌 Draw and practice labeling the diagrams of the Human Digestive System, Human Heart, and Nephron.
📌 Write down the overall chemical equation for Photosynthesis.
📌 Remember: Arteries carry blood AWAY from the heart, Veins carry blood TOWARDS the heart.
quick_recap: ⭐ Villi in the small intestine increase surface area for maximum absorption of digested food.
⭐ The breakdown of glucose always starts in the cytoplasm, forming pyruvate.
⭐ Artificial kidney (Hemodialysis) is used to filter blood for patients with kidney failure.
